documents.notes: THE KEY JURISDICTIONAL-SPLIT RULE. Wastes from oil, gas, and geothermal E&P activities subject to RRC regulation remain under RRC jurisdiction even when processed/treated/disposed of at a TCEQ-authorized Ch. 330 solid waste facility. documents.notes: Pipeline eminent-domain authority in Texas turns on 'common carrier' status: a company owning/operating pipelines transporting crude oil, coal, carbon dioxide, or hydrogen for hire, or transporting crude purchased from others, is a common carrier under §§111.002/111.003/111.0013 and may condemn land/ROW/easements for pipeline construction under §111.019. §111.0194 sets the standard statutory pipeline easement width at 50 feet. A pipeline operator DECLARES common-carrier status on its Form T-4 permit application (see tx-rrc-pipeline-t4-pops in tx-west.yaml) — but per Texas Rice Land Partners v. Denbury Green Pipeline-Texas (Tex. 2012 line of cases), that T-4 declaration is NOT irrefutable/conclusive proof of common-carrier status; it can be challenged and the operator must show a reasonable probability the pipeline will at some point transport gas/oil for third parties (not solely its own production) to sustain eminent-domain authority.
